integrity: The bracket and Rota-Baxter identity are reconstructed independently from the primary source's Example 2.11. The proof partitions the complete solution set by the bottom row of the operator matrix and isolates the sole characteristic-two enlargement. A standalone checker exhaustively verifies every operator over F2 and F3 and replays the stratum counts over several prime fields.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns one fixed three-dimensional 3-Leibniz algebra and counts operators without quotienting by automorphisms.
The finite-field theorem is obtained by direct reconstruction of the defining polynomial equations; it is not asserted for arbitrary 3-Leibniz algebras.
A specialized or unindexed finite-field calculation may contain an equivalent formula.
title: Finite-field Rota–Baxter census for a three-dimensional \(3\)-Leibniz algebra
